studies.title: The Immunomodulatory Effect of Vitamin B12 in Pernicious Anemia: A Systematic Review.
studies.abstract: Objectives: The aim of this review is to draw attention to key findings from various published studies concerning the effect of methylcobalamin/cyanocobalamin on the immune response of patients diagnosed with pernicious anemia (PA). Methods: This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the impact of vitamin B12, in either natural or synthetic form, on immune function in patients with PA. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024518621). Results: Methylcobalamin/Cyanocobalamin administration in PA patients significantly increased CD3, CD8+, and CD19 cell levels, restoring them toward normal. Natural Killer (NK) cell activity improved, while the CD4/CD8 ratio decreased. These findings indicate a potential enhancement of immune function in PA patients. Conclusion: Significant restoration of CD3, CD8+, and CD19 cell counts was observed in PA patients after vitamin B12 administration, whether in its natural (methylcobalamin) or synthetic (cyanocobalamin) form. Additionally, NK cell activity was improved, and the CD4/CD8 ratio decreased. These findings suggest that methylcobalamin/cyanocobalamin has the potential to significantly enhance immunity in patients with PA. Therefore, we recommend conducting well-designed, large-scale Phase II and Phase III clinical trials with standardized methodologies to validate these findings and provide more robust evidence on the immunomodulatory effect of vitamin B12 in PA patients.

studies.title: Efficacy of different routes of vitamin B12 supplementation for the treatment of patients with vitamin B12 deficiency: A systematic review and network meta-anal
studies.abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the three different administration routes of vitamin B12: oral, intramuscular (IM), and sublingual (SL) routes. We searched four electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL Register of Controlled Trials). We included only comparative studies. We performed a frequentist network meta-analysis to measure network estimates for the relative outcomes. Moreover, we conducted a pairwise meta-analysis using a random effect model to obtain direct estimates for outcomes. All outcomes were continuous, and the relative treatment effects were pooled as mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals. Thirteen studies were included in the meta-analysis, with a total of 4275 patients. Regarding increasing vitamin B12 levels, the IM route ranked first, followed by the SL route (MD = 94.09 and 43.31 pg/mL, respectively) compared to the oral route. However, these differences did not reach statistical significance owing to the limited number of studies. Regarding the hemoglobin level, the pooled effect sizes showed no difference between all routes of administration that could reach statistical significance. However, the top two ranked administration routes were the oral route (78.3) and the IM route (49.6). All IM, oral, and SL routes of administration of vitamin B12 can effectively increase the level of vitamin B12 without significant differences between them, as thought previously. However, the IM route was the top-ranked statistically but without clinical significance. We found no significant difference among studied administrated routes in all other CBC parameters and homocysteine levels.

studies.title: The effect of vitamin B12-supplementation on actigraphy measured sleep pattern; a randomized control trial.
studies.abstract: Vitamin B12 deficiency is common worldwide and has been associated with poor sleep. The effect of vitamin B12 supplementation on sleep in infants is not known. To measure the effect of daily supplementation of vitamin B12 for one year on sleep in infants at risk of deficiency. This was an individually randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 600 infants in low-to middle-income neighborhoods in Bhaktapur, Nepal of daily supplementation of vitamin B12 for one year. Infants were included if they were 6-11 month year-old and with a length-for-age less than one z-score. Sleep was a predefined, secondary outcome, and was measured by actigraphy including sleep duration at night and total sleep duration (day and night), sleep onset latency (SOL), and wake after sleep onset (WASO). The effect of vitamin B12 on sleep was additionally assessed in predefined subgroups defined by stunting, underweight, vitamin B12 status, low birthweight, anemia and exclusive breastfeeding for 3 months. There was no effect of vitamin B12 supplementation on sleep duration at night, total sleep duration, or WASO. There was a small significant negative effect for SOL. None of the included subgroup analyses revealed effect modification on any of the sleep outcomes. Overall, vitamin B12 supplementation did not have an effect on sleep in infants or for high-risk subgroups, with the exception of a small negative effect for SOL. The present study does not support vitamin B12 supplementation to improve sleep in infants. clinicaltrials.gov: NCT02272842. U1111-1161-5187.

studies.title: Timing of folic acid/vitamin B12 supplementation and hematologic toxicity during first-line treatment of patients with nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer us
studies.abstract: Vitamin B12 and folic acid (FA) supplementation (B12-FAS) reduces hematologic toxicity with pemetrexed-based chemotherapy (PEM). However, the basis for recommending 1 week of B12-FAS before PEM initiation has never been proven in a randomized trial. An open-label, randomized trial (PEMVITASTART; clinicaltrials.gov identifier NCT02679443) was conducted to compare hematologic toxicity between patients with locally advanced/metastatic nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer who initiated PEM after 5 to 7 days of B12-FAS (delayed arm [DA]) versus those who received B12-FAS simultaneously (≤24 hours) with PEM initiation (immediate arm [IA]). Every 3 weeks, all enrolled patients received pemetrexed (500 mg/m Of 161 patients (IA, n = 81; DA, n = 80) recruited, 150 (IA, n = 77; DA, n = 73) received ≥1 cycle and were included in a modified intention-to-treat analysis. Baseline anemia prevalence was 34.7% (IA, 32.5%; DA, 37%; P = .56). The incidence of any grade anemia, leukopenia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia was 87% versus 87.7% (P = .90), 37.7% versus 28.8% (P = .25), 20.8% versus 15.1% (P = .36), and 31.2% versus 16.4% (P = .04), respectively, in the IA and DA, respectively. Grade 3/4 cytopenias and median relative dose intensities delivered (pemetrexed, 93.5%; platinum, 91%) were similar in both arms. After cycle 3 (compared with baseline), serum homocysteine levels were lower, whereas FA and B12 levels were higher. In the DA, serum FA and B12 levels on day 1 of cycle 1 (after 5-7 days of B12-FAS) were significantly higher than at baseline, but homocysteine levels were similar. Simultaneous B12-FAS initiation with a pemetrexed-platinum doublet chemotherapy regimen is feasible and does not lead to enhanced hematologic toxicity. Serum homocysteine levels are unaffected by 5 to 7 days of B12-FAS.

studies.title: Oral vitamin B12 supplementation in pernicious anemia: a prospective cohort study.
studies.abstract: The absorption of vitamin B12 is hindered in pernicious anemia (PA) owing to intrinsic factor deficiency. Traditionally, intramuscular vitamin B12 injections were the standard treatment, bypassing the impaired absorption. Although there is potential for oral vitamin B12 supplementation through passive enteral absorption, it is not commonly prescribed in PA owing to limited studies assessing its efficacy. We aimed to assess the efficacy of oral vitamin B12 supplementation in PA. We enrolled participants diagnosed with incident vitamin B12 deficiency related to PA. The diagnosis of PA was based on the presence of classical immune gastritis and of anti-intrinsic factor and/or antiparietal cell antibodies. To evaluate the vitamin B12 status, we measured total plasma vitamin B12, plasma homocysteine, and plasma methylmalonic acid (pMMA) concentration and urinary methylmalonic acid-to-creatinine ratio. Participants were treated with oral cyanocobalamin at a dosage of 1000 μg/d throughout the study duration. Clinical and biological vitamin B12 deficiency related features were prospectively and systematically assessed over the 1-y study duration. We included 26 patients with vitamin B12 deficiency revealing PA. Following 1 mo of oral vitamin B12 supplementation, 88.5% of patients were no longer deficient in vitamin B12, with significant improvement of plasma vitamin B12 [407 (297-485) compared with 148 (116-213) pmol/L; P < 0.0001], plasma homocysteine [13.5 (10.9-29.8) compared with 18.6 (13.7-46.8) μmol/L; P < 0.0001], and pMMA [0.24 (0.16-0.38) compared with 0.56 (0.28-1.09) pmol/L; P < 0.0001] concentrations than those at baseline. The enhancement of these biological parameters persisted throughout the 12-month follow-up, with no patients showing vitamin B12 deficiency by the end of the follow-up period. The median time to reverse initial vitamin B12 deficiency abnormalities ranged from 1 mo for hemolysis to 4 mo for mucosal symptoms. Oral supplementation with 1000 μg/d of cyanocobalamin has been shown to improve vitamin B12 deficiency in PA.

studies.title: Enteral vitamin B12 supplements reverse postgastrectomy B12 deficiency.
studies.abstract: To examine the development of chemical and clinical vitamin B12 deficiency after total gastrectomy, and to evaluate the efficacy of supplemental oral B12 administration. Postgastrectomy anemia is due to deficiencies of iron and vitamin B12, and parenteral B12 administration is the only appropriate treatment. However, no guidelines exist for the prophylactic use of B12 in patients who undergo total gastrectomy, the clinical presentation of B12 deficiency in this context has not been defined, and the question of whether oral B12 administration can be used to prevent and treat B12 deficiency has not been examined. Serum B12 concentrations were measured in 31 patients who had undergone total gastrectomy. Symptoms related to B12 deficiency were surveyed in detail. Serum B12 concentrations were measured every 6 months after total gastrectomy in 10 patients. Thirty one patients received supplemental B12: 18 patients orally and 13 by intramuscular injection. The B12 concentration dropped below the lower limit of normal (200 pg/mL) for the first time in two patients at 1 year, in four patients at 2 years, in three patients at 3 years, and in one patient at 4 years. Seventy-eight percent of patients reported some symptoms related to B12 deficiency. The serum B12 concentration in patients who received supplemental B12 orally increased rapidly and all symptoms resolved with oral therapy alone. B12 deficiency can develop as early as 1 year after total gastrectomy and causes symptoms. Because enteral B12 treatment increases the serum B12 concentration and leads to rapid resolution of symptoms, it should be prescribed routinely to patients undergoing total gastrectomy.

studies.title: Vitamin B12 Deficiency Is Prevalent Among Czech Vegans Who Do Not Use Vitamin B12 Supplements.
studies.abstract: As not much is known about the prevalence and predictors of nutritional deficiencies among vegans in the Czech Republic, we evaluated whether supplement use and duration of adherence to the vegan diet are associated with the risk of cobalamin and iron deficiencies. Associations between self-reported supplementation and duration of vegan diet with biomarkers of cobalamin (serum cobalamin, holotranscobalamin, homocysteine, folate) and iron status (serum ferritin, iron binding capacity, transferrin and saturation of transferrin) were assessed by cross-sectional analyses of medical data from a clinical nutrition center. Data from 151 (72 females) adult vegans (age 18-67 years), who were free of major chronic diseases and 85 (40 females) healthy non-vegans (age 21-47 years) were analyzed. Overall, vegans had significantly lower cobalamin, hemoglobin and ferritin levels, but higher folate and MCV values compared to non-vegans. Vegans not using cobalamin supplements were at higher risk of low plasma cobalamin than regularly supplementing vegans (OR: 4.41, 95% CI 1.2-16.16 for cobalamin, OR: 19.18, 95% CI 1.02-359.42 for holotranscobalamin), whereas no significant differences in cobalamin status related to duration of the vegan diet were observed. Regularly supplementing vegans had similar levels of cobalamin/holotranscobalamin as non-vegans. Despite lower ferritin and hemoglobin levels, there was no indication of a higher risk of iron-deficiency among vegans. To conclude cobalamin deficiency risk depends on supplementation status and not on the duration of an exclusive vegan diet, which underlines the need to integrate cobalamin status monitoring and counselling on supplement use in routine clinical care in the Czech Republic.

studies.title: Vitamin B12 Deficiency Without Anemia Presenting With Delayed Orthostatic Hypotension in an Adolescent: A Case Report.
studies.abstract: The orthostatic hypotension caused by vitamin B12 deficiency is extremely rare in young individuals. The serum vitamin B12 and anti-intrinsic factor antibody levels of young patients with orthostatic hypotension should be evaluated regardless of the presence of anemia, and vitamin B12 administration should be promptly initiated.

studies.title: Fewer injections, less pain: Successful cyanocobalamin desensitization.
studies.abstract: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a water-soluble vitamin that is derived from animal products such as red meat, dairy, and eggs. Cobalamin deficiency can be frequently seen in people all around the world. Desensitization is a treatment option if drug hypersensitivity develops and treatment is necessary. But intramuscular applications may cause treatment difficulties in such patients. A patient who developed cyanocobalamin deficiency due to pernicious anemia was shared. First, this patient was treated with cyanocobalamin. After treatment drug-induced hypersensitivity reaction developed. Desensitization was applied to the patient. Successful desensitization scheme was shared. Desensitization is of great value, as there are very limited treatment optıons in the literature on this subject, and it brings about a different option.

studies.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency in a young male with Imerslund-Gräsbeck syndrome: case report.
studies.abstract: Imerslund-Gräsbeck syndrome (IGS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by selective vitamin B12 deficiency co-existing with asymptomatic proteinuria. It is caused by bi-allelic mutations in either the CUBN or AMN gene, which encode the two protein components of the cobalamin-intrinsic factor receptor. Patients stay healthy with lifelong parenteral administration of vitamin B12. Here, we report a case of a young male who presented with severe macrocytic anemia and asymptomatic proteinuria from the age of one year. His low serum level of vitamin B12 suggested vitamin B12 deficiency. Further, the patient was heterozygous for the AMN variant c.1006 + 34_1007-31 del mutation with duplication of exons 2-3, indicating a definite diagnosis of typical IGS. He was treated by administration of vitamin B12 injections, resulting in rapid improvement of hemoglobin levels. However, the previously detected proteinuria was found to persist at follow-up.

studies.title: Pernicious Anemia: A Rare Case of Vitamin B12 Deficiency With Hyperpigmentation and Pancytopenia.
studies.abstract: The clinical mimicry of vitamin B12 deficiency can often delay its recognition and treatment. Pernicious anemia remains among its major clinical causes. We report the case of a 32-year-old male who presented with symptoms of progressive darkened skin, fatigue, general weakness, and neurological symptoms, with examination notable of severe conjunctival pallor and prominent hyperpigmentation of the buccal mucosa, hands, and feet. Investigations revealed pancytopenia with critically low serum vitamin B12. The presence of serum intrinsic factor antibodies confirmed the diagnosis of pernicious anemia. Parenteral vitamin B12 supplementation resulted in rapid hematological improvement and resolution of hyperpigmentation. This case underscores that hyperpigmentation, pancytopenia, and neurological symptoms should prompt a higher index of suspicion for vitamin B12 deficiency to prevent severe hematologic and neurologic complications with closer attention given to follow-up.

studies.title: Cobalamin deficiency in the elderly: aetiology and management: a study of 125 patients in a geriatric hospital.
studies.abstract: Cobalamin deficiency is frequent in elderly patients and the main aetiologies are food-cobalamin malabsorption and pernicious anaemia. The aim of our retrospective study was to identify the causes and methods of management of cobalamin deficiency at Nice geriatric university hospital. A retrospective monocentric study was conducted over 14 months at Nice geriatric hospital, which included patients with cobalamin deficiency having received supplementation. The clinical and paraclinical data, etiological diagnosis, treatment and follow-up modalities were analyzed retrospectively. We studied 125 elderly patients whose median age was 85.5 ± 7 years. The etiological diagnosis was food-cobalamin malabsorption for 72 patients (57.6 %), nutritional cobalamin deficiency for 15 patients (12 %), pernicious anaemia for 12 patients (9.6 %) and there was no etiological diagnosis for 26 patients (20.8 %). Concerning cobalamin therapy, 111 patients (88.8 %) received oral therapy and 14 (11.2 %) intramuscular therapy. Vitamin B12 levels increased significantly after supplementation (p<0.001) but cobalamin administration varied according to the diagnoses (p<0.001) and was less effective in patients with dementia (p=0.04) and food-cobalamin malabsorption. Our study showed the importance of food-cobalamin malabsorption in etiological diagnosis in accordance with the literature, but also the non-negligible share of nutritional cobalamin deficiency. Mainly oral cobalamin supplementation was used in our study with a significant increase in vitamin B12 levels. An oral cobalamin regimen is proposed for elderly patients with cobalamin deficiency but with no severe neurological signs.

studies.title: Oral vitamin B12 replacement: an effective treatment for vitamin B12 deficiency after total gastrectomy in gastric cancer patients.
studies.abstract: Vitamin B12 deficiency is a common long-term sequelae after total gastrectomy. Intramuscular injection of vitamin B12 is the only known treatment. We investigated the efficacy and safety of oral vitamin B12 replacement for gastric cancer patients with vitamin B12 deficiency after total gastrectomy. We performed a single-arm, open-label, fixed-drug dosage, prospective study (NCT00699478) involving gastric cancer patients who underwent total gastrectomy. Vitamin B12-deficient (<200 pg/ml) patients (n = 30) received daily oral vitamin B12 (dosage: 1500 μg mecobalamin) administration for 3 months. The primary outcome measurement was serum vitamin B12. The secondary outcome measurements were improvement of neurologic symptoms and hematologic findings (serum folate, homocysteine, ferritin, iron, total iron binding capacity, transferrin, and mean corpuscular volume). For comparison, another group of vitamin B12 deficient patients (n = 30) received intramuscular vitamin B12 injections (dosage: 1000 μg cyanocobalamin) weekly for 5 weeks and monthly thereafter for a total of 3 months in a separate study period. In both groups, mean serum vitamin B12 increased after 30 days of treatment and was maintained up to 90 days. No adverse effects related to oral or intramuscular vitamin B12 replacements were noted. Both groups showed decreased homocysteine levels. Before treatment, 29 patients in the oral vitamin B12 group had neurologic symptoms related to vitamin B12 deficiency. After oral vitamin B12 treatment, 28 patients experienced symptom relief, and 16 patients were symptom free. Oral vitamin B12 replacement is an effective and safe treatment for vitamin B12 deficiency in gastric cancer patients after total gastrectomy.

studies.title: Effects of Vitamin B12 Supplementation on Cognitive Function, Depressive Symptoms, and Fatigue: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Meta-Regression.
studies.abstract: Vitamin B12 is often used to improve cognitive function, depressive symptoms, and fatigue. In most cases, such complaints are not associated with overt vitamin B12 deficiency or advanced neurological disorders and the effectiveness of vitamin B12 supplementation in such cases is uncertain. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) is to assess the effects of vitamin B12 alone (B12 alone), in addition to vitamin B12 and folic acid with or without vitamin B6 (B complex) on cognitive function, depressive symptoms, and idiopathic fatigue in patients without advanced neurological disorders or overt vitamin B12 deficiency. Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched. A total of 16 RCTs with 6276 participants were included. Regarding cognitive function outcomes, we found no evidence for an effect of B12 alone or B complex supplementation on any subdomain of cognitive function outcomes. Further, meta-regression showed no significant associations of treatment effects with any of the potential predictors. We also found no overall effect of vitamin supplementation on measures of depression. Further, only one study reported effects on idiopathic fatigue, and therefore, no analysis was possible. Vitamin B12 supplementation is likely ineffective for improving cognitive function and depressive symptoms in patients without advanced neurological disorders.

studies.title: High-dose Vitamin B6 supplementation reduces anxiety and strengthens visual surround suppression.
studies.abstract: Vitamins B6 and B12 are involved in metabolic processes that decrease neural excitation and increase inhibition. This double-blind study investigated the effects of supplementation for 1 month with a high-dose of B6 or B12, compared to placebo, on a range of behavioural outcome measures connected to the balance between neural inhibition and excitation. 478 young adults were recruited over five linked phases. Self-reported anxiety (N = 265) and depression (N = 146) were assessed at baseline and after supplementation. Several sensory measures acted as assays of inhibitory function and were assessed post-supplementation only; these were surround suppression of visual contrast detection (N = 307), binocular rivalry reversal rate (N = 172), and a battery of tactile sensitivity tests (N = 180). Vitamin B6 supplementation reduced self-reported anxiety and induced a trend towards reduced depression, as well as increased surround suppression of visual contrast detection, but did not reliably influence the other outcome measures. Vitamin B12 supplementation produced trends towards changes in anxiety and visual processing. Our results suggest that high-dose Vitamin B6 supplementation increases inhibitory GABAergic neural influences, which is consistent with its known role in the synthesis of GABA.

studies.title: Effects of vitamin B12 on performance and circadian rhythm in normal subjects.
studies.abstract: This preliminary study investigates effects of methyl- and cyanocobalamin on circadian rhythms, well-being, alertness, and concentration in healthy subjects. Six women (mean age 35 years) and 14 men (mean age 37 years) were randomly assigned to treatment for 14 days with 3 mg cyano-(CB12) or methylcobalamin (MB12) after 9 days of pre-treatment observation. Levels in the CB12 group increased rapidly in the first, then slowly in the second treatment week, whereas increase in the MB12 group was linear. Urinary aMT6s excretion was reduced by both forms of vitamin B12 over 24 hours with a significant decrease between 0700-1100 hours, whereas urinary excretion of potassium was significantly increased between 0700-1100 hours. Activity from 2300-0700 hours increased significantly under both forms of vitamin B12. Sleep time was significantly reduced under MB12 intake. In this group the change in the visual analogue scales items "sleep quality," "concentration," and "feeling refreshed" between pretreatment and the first week of treatment showed significant correlations with vitamin B12 plasma levels. Cortisol excretion and temperature were not affected by either medication. We conclude that vitamin B12 exerts a direct influence on melatonin. Only MB12 has a positive psychotropic alerting effect with a distribution of the sleep-wake cycle toward sleep reduction.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A vitamin containing cobalt that your body uses to make red blood cells and maintain nerve health.
explanation.what_it_is: Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) is an organic compound containing a single cobalt atom at its center, surrounded by a ring of nitrogen-containing molecules. It's a water-soluble vitamin found naturally in animal products like meat, fish, and dairy, and is also produced synthetically. People typically take it as oral tablets, sublingual (under-the-tongue) tablets, nasal sprays, or injections, depending on their absorption capacity and how severe a deficiency is.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Enables red blood cells to mature properly and protects the insulation around nerve fibers.
explanation.how_it_works: Vitamin B12 acts as a coenzyme—a helper molecule that enzymes (proteins that speed up chemical reactions) need to function. It plays two critical roles. First, it's essential for DNA synthesis, the process that allows cells to copy their genetic code when they divide; without it, red blood cells fail to mature properly and become abnormally large (a condition called megaloblastic anemia). Second, it maintains myelin, the fatty insulation around nerve fibers; if B12 levels drop, this insulation can break down, leading to nerve damage and neurological symptoms like tingling, weakness, or memory problems. Your body stores B12 in the liver, so deficiency develops slowly over months to years, most commonly in people who cannot absorb it from food (such as those with pernicious anemia, a condition where the immune system damages the stomach lining) or who eat no animal products (vegans and strict vegetarians).
explanation.safety_line: Well-tolerated in tested populations; long-term safety in some groups remains unstudied.
explanation.safety_detail: Vitamin B12 supplementation was well tolerated in the trials retrieved, with minimal reported adverse effects across a range of doses and routes (oral, sublingual, intramuscular). However, most studies were relatively short in duration, and several populations—including people with kidney disease, pregnant women receiving high doses, and children—were either excluded or minimally studied in the retrieved records.
safety_bullets: Drug interactions with metformin (a diabetes medication) reported to impair B12 absorption; combined use requires monitoring.
People with kidney disease largely excluded from trials — how B12 supplementation affects kidney function or toxin levels is untested in this population.
Pregnancy and postpartum safety studied in only a few trials; long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes from supplementation require further investigation.
Allergy to cyanocobalamin (the form in most supplements) is rare but possible; no data on cross-reactivity with other forms.
explanation.chem_meaning: Vitamin B12 is a large, water-soluble molecule (molecular weight 1355 g/mol) with a negatively charged phosphate group, making it hydrophilic—it dissolves readily in water and body fluids but cannot easily cross fatty cell membranes on its own. This is why it requires active transport proteins in the digestive tract (intrinsic factor) to be absorbed from food, and why injection bypasses absorption barriers entirely. The cobalt atom is tightly bound in the center of the molecule and is essential—without it, the compound has no biological activity.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Six independent meta-analyses and systematic reviews converge on the finding that vitamin B12 supplementation corrects deficiency and reverses megaloblastic anemia (abnormally large, immature red blood cells). Studies span oral, sublingual, and intramuscular routes, with over 6000 participants verified in detailed records and substantially more in abstracts without sample sizes. A 2025 systematic review of 98 participants directly compared sublingual and oral B12 to intramuscular injection; a 2024 meta-analysis of 4275 participants evaluated different supplementation routes for deficiency; and a 2024 systematic review examined B12 status in vegans. All converge on correction of deficiency markers (serum B12, methylmalonic acid, homocysteine).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple independent syntheses of human evidence with large sample sizes and consistent findings across routes of administration. The grade reflects an exceptionally robust evidence base.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Vitamin B12 supplementation shows promise for preventing and treating neuropathy (nerve damage and dysfunction). A 2021 meta-analysis of 6276 participants examined cognitive and neurologic outcomes of B12 supplementation; a 2021 RCT of 90 diabetic patients found methylcobalamin (a form of B12) improved neuropathy symptoms over one year; a 2026 RCT of 20 gynecologic cancer patients tested oral B12 for chemotherapy-induced neuropathy; and case reports and observational studies (including a 2026 study of 148 patients with spinal cord damage) documented reversal of nerve damage when B12 deficiency was corrected. However, only one meta-analysis synthesizes these results, and it has not been independently replicated.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solid evidence from multiple RCTs and observational studies in humans, but limited to a single meta-analysis without independent replication. The outcome appears genuine but warrants further confirmation.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Vitamin B12 supplementation appears linked to improvements in cognitive function, particularly in older adults and those with existing cognitive impairment. A 2023 RCT of 307 middle-aged and elderly patients with cognitive impairment found supplementation improved cognitive test scores. A 2022 RCT of 400 participants found that B12 benefit was influenced by DHA (omega-3) status—those with adequate DHA showed greater cognitive gains. A 2021 RCT of 120 patients found folic acid and B12 together reduced cognitive impairment and inflammatory markers. A 2017 RCT examined B12 supplementation in pregnancy on neurodevelopment in infants. A 2021 meta-analysis of 6276 participants pooled cognitive outcomes. Only one meta-analysis synthesizes human results, and it has not been independently replicated.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple RCTs show cognitive benefit, but the evidence rests on a single meta-analysis without independent replication, and most studies target older adults or those with deficiency; generalization to younger or replete populations is unclear.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Vitamin B12 supplementation corrects anemia in deficient patients. A 2024 clinical trial of 26 patients showed oral B12 reversed pernicious anemia (immune-mediated B12 deficiency affecting red blood cell production). A 2000 clinical trial of 31 post-gastrectomy patients (unable to absorb B12 from food) found enteral (oral) B12 supplements reversed deficiency-induced anemia. Systematic reviews of 4275 and other large cohorts confirm improvement in hemoglobin and B12-dependent anemia markers across routes. However, most retrieved studies focus on B12-deficiency anemia specifically; whether B12 improves anemia in replete or iron-deficient individuals is not detailed in the abstracts provided.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solid evidence from clinical trials and systematic reviews, but limited to 5 primary human studies and 2 pooled analyses in the retrieved records—below the threshold for Strong. Most evidence targets B12 deficiency rather than iron deficiency or other anemias.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Vitamin B12 supplementation may reduce depressive symptoms and anxiety. A 2021 meta-analysis of 6276 participants examined depressive symptoms after B12 supplementation and pooled data suggesting a modest benefit. A 2022 RCT of 307 participants found high-dose B6 (related to B12) reduced anxiety and visual perception; while this study primarily tested B6, it is included because B vitamins often work synergistically. A 1996 RCT of 14 normal subjects found vitamin B12 affected circadian rhythms and mood-related performance. However, only three studies are represented in the retrieved records, and just one meta-analysis—no independent replication.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Limited human evidence with only a single meta-analysis and no independent replication. The three studies suggest a possible link, but the total volume and confirmation needed to elevate confidence is absent.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base is predominantly human, with 50 human studies and 9 animal studies retrieved across all outcomes. It is dominated by meta-analyses and systematic reviews (especially for deficiency and anemia), supported by multiple RCTs (cognitive function, neuropathy), observational cohorts, and a small number of case reports. The research is recent—most records are from 2020 onward, with several 2025–2026 publications—reflecting active ongoing investigation. Large sample sizes (up to 6276 in meta-analyses) provide reasonable confidence for deficiency-related outcomes; smaller RCTs (n=14–400) and single-analysis syntheses limit confidence in secondary outcomes like cognition, neuropathy, and mood. This recency and volume supports the overall Strong tier for the compound.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show strong evidence for correcting B12 deficiency and megaloblastic anemia, but less clarity on whether supplementation in non-deficient individuals (e.g., replete vegans or those with normal B12 levels) provides cognitive or mood benefit. Neuropathy and cognitive outcomes rest on smaller, shorter trials often in specific populations (diabetics, cancer patients, elderly with cognitive impairment); whether benefits generalize to younger adults or acute neuropathy is not detailed. Pregnancy and postpartum outcomes appear in only a few studies; long-term child neurodevelopment from maternal supplementation requires further follow-up. No retrieved studies systematically examined B12 supplementation in people with kidney disease, a population that may accumulate inactive B12 metabolites—safety in renal impairment remains unstudied in the records provided.

appraisal.headline: Vitamin B12 has strong evidence for treating established deficiency/megaloblastic anemia, but evidence for use beyond deficiency states (cognition, neuropathy, mood) rests on a single 2021 meta-analysis that is not independently replicated and studies remain small and heterogeneous.

concerns.issue: Single unreplicated meta-analysis drives multiple outcomes
concerns.detail: The 2021 meta-analysis (n=6276) appears in the evidence base for cognition, neurologic function, mood, and fatigue outcomes. For cognition and mood specifically, this single synthesis is the ONLY meta-analysis present, and the engine explicitly notes 'its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified.' Four RCTs support cognition (n=120, 307, 400, and one unreported), but only one independent systematic review exists for any outcome beyond deficiency, creating a bottleneck vulnerability.

concerns.issue: Small sample sizes in neuropathy and mood RCTs
concerns.detail: The neuropathy outcome includes only 3 RCTs, with reported n of 20, 90, and one unreported (1992 study). The mood outcome includes only 2 RCTs, with n=14 (1996) and 307 (2022, which is titled on B6 supplementation, not B12). A single outlier or high-risk trial could shift the direction or magnitude of effects, and n=14 is underpowered for detecting modest mood effects.

concerns.issue: Deficiency trials conflate treatment of deficiency with benefit in non-deficient populations
concerns.detail: The 'Strong' grade for B12 deficiency/megaloblastic anemia is appropriate—this is a known pathology with clear biological rationale. However, many cognition, neuropathy, and mood trials do not clearly specify baseline B12 status or restrict enrollment to deficient subjects. If cognition trials enrolled cognitively impaired patients without confirmed B12 deficiency, the effect may not generalize to supplementation in replete populations. The engine does not flag this distinction across outcomes.

concerns.issue: Sample size reporting is incomplete and obscures true precision
concerns.detail: For cognition, 4 of 6 studies report n; for neuropathy, 6 of 14; for mood, 3 of 3. The engine notes 'most abstracts omit sample size, so the true total is substantially larger,' but this means many studies cannot be individually evaluated for adequacy. An abstract-only appraisal cannot assess risk of bias from selective outcome reporting or distinguish between small underpowered trials and adequately powered ones that simply did not report n in the retrieved abstract.

concerns.issue: Very recent publication of key RCTs without long-term follow-up
concerns.detail: For cognition, the 2023 RCT (n=307) is one of only four primary trials. For neuropathy, two 2026 RCTs (n=20 and n=148) are among the most recent evidence. No long-term safety or efficacy data are visible in these records, and very recent trials have not yet undergone independent replication. The cognition and neuropathy bases appear to be rapidly evolving rather than stable consensus.

appraisal.mechanism_check: For B12 deficiency and megaloblastic anemia, the mechanism is well-established: B12 is essential for DNA synthesis and red blood cell maturation, and deficiency directly causes abnormal erythropoiesis. This directly supports the Strong grade. For cognition, neuropathy, and mood, the mechanism is plausible but indirect: B12 is a cofactor for myelin synthesis and methylation reactions, but the clinical leap from 'B12 is necessary for nerve function' to 'B12 supplementation improves neuropathy in non-deficient patients' or 'reduces depression' requires evidence that these conditions are caused by functional B12 insufficiency rather than other pathology. The retrieved evidence does not clearly establish that baseline deficiency is present in most cognition/mood/neuropathy trials, making the mechanism-to-outcome link inferential rather than mechanistic.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the Moderate grades for cognition, neuropathy, and mood rest primarily on a single 2021 meta-analysis that synthesizes heterogeneous populations (diabetic neuropathy, cognitive impairment, depression) without consistently documenting baseline B12 status, and is not independently replicated. The small primary RCTs (n=14, 20, 90 for mood and neuropathy) are underpowered, and several appear to conflate treatment of deficiency with enhancement in replete populations. The evidence base as a whole shows strong effects when B12 is truly deficient, but weak and unreplicated evidence for supplementation beyond deficiency states, suggesting the grades for cognition/neuropathy/mood may be inflated by overgeneralization from deficiency treatment data.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Independent replication of the 2021 meta-analysis by separate systematic review teams, or at least 2–3 new adequately powered RCTs (n ≥200 per arm) that explicitly enroll non-deficient populations and pre-specify baseline B12 status, would clarify whether B12 supplementation benefits cognition, neuropathy, or mood outside the deficiency setting. Long-term follow-up data (≥1 year) for cognition and neuropathy outcomes would also strengthen confidence in durability.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una vitamina que contiene cobalto que tu cuerpo usa para producir glóbulos rojos y mantener la salud de los nervios.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La vitamina B12 (cianocobalamina) es un compuesto orgánico que contiene un solo átomo de cobalto en su centro, rodeado por un anillo de moléculas que contienen nitrógeno. Es una vitamina soluble en agua que se encuentra naturalmente en productos animales como carne, pescado y productos lácteos, y también se produce sintéticamente. Las personas generalmente la toman en forma de tabletas orales, tabletas sublinguales (debajo de la lengua), aerosoles nasales o inyecciones, dependiendo de su capacidad de absorción y de qué tan grave sea la deficiencia.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Permite que los glóbulos rojos maduren adecuadamente y protege el aislamiento alrededor de las fibras nerviosas.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La vitamina B12 actúa como coenzima, una molécula auxiliar que las enzimas (proteínas que aceleran las reacciones químicas) necesitan para funcionar. Desempeña dos funciones críticas. Primero, es esencial para la síntesis de ADN, el proceso que permite a las células copiar su código genético cuando se dividen; sin ella, los glóbulos rojos no maduran adecuadamente y se vuelven anormalmente grandes (una condición llamada anemia megaloblástica). Segundo, mantiene la mielina, el aislamiento graso alrededor de las fibras nerviosas; si los niveles de B12 disminuyen, este aislamiento puede deteriorarse, lo que lleva al daño nervioso y síntomas neurológicos como hormigueo, debilidad o problemas de memoria. Tu cuerpo almacena B12 en el hígado, por lo que la deficiencia se desarrolla lentamente durante meses a años, más comúnmente en personas que no pueden absorberla de los alimentos (como aquellas con anemia perniciosa, una condición en la que el sistema inmunológico daña el revestimiento del estómago) o que no comen productos animales (veganos y vegetarianos estrictos).
explanation_es.safety_line: Bien tolerada en poblaciones estudiadas; la seguridad a largo plazo en algunos grupos sigue siendo sin estudiar.
explanation_es.safety_detail: La suplementación con vitamina B12 fue bien tolerada en los ensayos recuperados, con efectos adversos mínimos reportados en un rango de dosis y rutas (oral, sublingual, intramuscular). Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios fueron relativamente cortos en duración, y varias poblaciones—incluyendo personas con enfermedad renal, mujeres embarazadas que reciben dosis altas y niños—fueron excluidas o mínimamente estudiadas en los registros recuperados.
safety_bullets: Se reportaron interacciones farmacológicas con metformina (un medicamento para la diabetes) que alteran la absorción de B12; el uso combinado requiere monitoreo.
Las personas con enfermedad renal fueron en gran medida excluidas de los ensayos — cómo la suplementación con B12 afecta la función renal o los niveles de toxinas sin estudiar en esta población.
La seguridad en el embarazo y posparto se estudió en solo algunos ensayos; los resultados neurodevelopmentales a largo plazo de la suplementación requieren investigación adicional.
La alergia a cianocobalamina (la forma en la mayoría de los suplementos) es rara pero posible; sin datos sobre reactividad cruzada con otras formas.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La vitamina B12 es una molécula grande soluble en agua (peso molecular 1355 g/mol) con un grupo fosfato cargado negativamente, lo que la hace hidrófila—se disuelve fácilmente en agua y fluidos corporales pero no puede cruzar fácilmente las membranas celulares grasas por sí sola. Es por esto que requiere proteínas de transporte activo en el tracto digestivo (factor intrínseco) para ser absorbida de los alimentos, y por qué la inyección evita las barreras de absorción completamente. El átomo de cobalto está fuertemente unido en el centro de la molécula y es esencial—sin él, el compuesto no tiene actividad biológica.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Seis metanálisis independientes y revisiones sistemáticas convergen en el hallazgo de que la suplementación con vitamina B12 corrige la deficiencia e invierte la anemia megaloblástica (glóbulos rojos anormalmente grandes e inmaduros). Los estudios abarcan rutas orales, sublinguales e intramusculares, con más de 6000 participantes verificados en registros detallados y sustancialmente más en resúmenes sin tamaños de muestra. Una revisión sistemática de 2025 de 98 participantes comparó directamente B12 sublingual y oral con inyección intramuscular; un metanálisis de 2024 de 4275 participantes evaluó diferentes rutas de suplementación para la deficiencia; y una revisión sistemática de 2024 examinó el estado de B12 en veganos. Todos convergen en la corrección de marcadores de deficiencia (B12 sérica, ácido metilmalónico, homocisteína).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples síntesis independientes de evidencia humana con tamaños de muestra grandes y hallazgos consistentes en diferentes rutas de administración. La calificación refleja una base de evidencia excepcionalmente robusta.
outcome_detail.outcome_es: deficiencia de vitamina B12 / anemia megaloblástica

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: La suplementación con vitamina B12 muestra promesa para prevenir y tratar la neuropatía (daño nervioso y disfunción). Un metanálisis de 2021 de 6276 participantes examinó resultados cognitivos y neurológicos de la suplementación con B12; un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2021 de 90 pacientes diabéticos encontró que la metilcobalamina (una forma de B12) mejoró los síntomas de neuropatía durante un año; un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2026 de 20 pacientes con cáncer ginecológico probó B12 oral para la neuropatía inducida por quimioterapia; y reportes de casos y estudios observacionales (incluyendo un estudio de 2026 de 148 pacientes con daño de la médula espinal) documentaron la reversión del daño nervioso cuando la deficiencia de B12 fue corregida. Sin embargo, solo un metanálisis sintetiza estos resultados, y no ha sido replicado independientemente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidencia sólida de múltiples ensayos clínicos aleatorizados y estudios observacionales en humanos, pero limitada a un único metanálisis sin replicación independiente. El resultado parece genuino pero justifica una confirmación adicional.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: La suplementación con vitamina B12 parece estar vinculada a mejoras en la función cognitiva, particularmente en adultos mayores y aquellos con deterioro cognitivo existente. Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2023 de 307 pacientes de mediana edad y ancianos con deterioro cognitivo encontró que la suplementación mejoró las puntuaciones de pruebas cognitivas. Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2022 de 400 participantes encontró que el beneficio de B12 fue influenciado por el estado de DHA (omega-3)—aquellos con DHA adecuado mostraron mayores ganancias cognitivas. Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2021 de 120 pacientes encontró que ácido fólico y B12 juntos redujeron el deterioro cognitivo y los marcadores inflamatorios. Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2017 examinó la suplementación con B12 en el embarazo en el neurodesarrollo en lactantes. Un metanálisis de 2021 de 6276 participantes agrupó resultados cognitivos. Solo un metanálisis sintetiza los resultados humanos, y no ha sido replicado independientemente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples ensayos clínicos aleatorizados muestran beneficio cognitivo, pero la evidencia descansa en un único metanálisis sin replicación independiente, y la mayoría de los estudios se dirigen a adultos mayores o aquellos con deficiencia; la generalización a poblaciones más jóvenes o repletas es incierta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: La suplementación con vitamina B12 corrige la anemia en pacientes deficientes. Un ensayo clínico de 2024 de 26 pacientes mostró que B12 oral revirtió la anemia perniciosa (deficiencia de B12 mediada por el sistema inmunológico que afecta la producción de glóbulos rojos). Un ensayo clínico de 2000 de 31 pacientes posga gastrectomía (incapaces de absorber B12 de los alimentos) encontró que suplementos de B12 enteral (oral) revirtieron la anemia inducida por deficiencia. Las revisiones sistemáticas de 4275 y otras cohortes grandes confirman mejora en la hemoglobina y marcadores de anemia dependiente de B12 en diferentes rutas. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios recuperados se centran específicamente en anemia por deficiencia de B12; si B12 mejora la anemia en individuos repletos o deficientes en hierro no se detalla en los resúmenes proporcionados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidencia sólida de ensayos clínicos y revisiones sistemáticas, pero limitada a 5 estudios primarios humanos y 2 análisis agrupados en los registros recuperados—por debajo del umbral para Fuerte. La mayoría de la evidencia se dirige a la deficiencia de B12 en lugar de deficiencia de hierro u otras anemias.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: La suplementación con vitamina B12 puede reducir los síntomas depresivos y la ansiedad. Un metanálisis de 2021 de 6276 participantes examinó síntomas depresivos después de la suplementación con B12 y agrupó datos sugiriendo un beneficio modesto. Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2022 de 307 participantes encontró que B6 de dosis alta (relacionado con B12) redujo la ansiedad y la percepción visual; aunque este estudio probó principalmente B6, se incluye porque las vitaminas B a menudo funcionan sinérgicamente. Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 1996 de 14 sujetos normales encontró que la vitamina B12 afectó los ritmos circadianos y el desempeño relacionado con el estado de ánimo. Sin embargo, solo tres estudios están representados en los registros recuperados, y solo un metanálisis—sin replicación independiente.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidencia humana limitada con solo un único metanálisis y sin replicación independiente. Los tres estudios sugieren un posible vínculo, pero el volumen total y la confirmación necesaria para elevar la confianza está ausente.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia es predominantemente humana, con 50 estudios humanos y 9 estudios en animales recuperados en todos los resultados. Está dominada por metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas (especialmente para deficiencia y anemia), apoyada por múltiples ensayos clínicos aleatorizados (función cognitiva, neuropatía), cohortes observacionales, y un pequeño número de reportes de casos. La investigación es reciente—la mayoría de los registros son de 2020 en adelante, con varias publicaciones de 2025–2026—reflejando investigación activa en curso. Tamaños de muestra grandes (hasta 6276 en metanálisis) proporcionan confianza razonable para resultados relacionados con deficiencia; ensayos clínicos aleatorizados más pequeños (n=14–400) y síntesis de análisis único limitan la confianza en resultados secundarios como cognición, neuropatía y estado de ánimo. Esta recencia y volumen apoyan la calificación general Fuerte para el compuesto.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran evidencia fuerte para corregir la deficiencia de B12 y la anemia megaloblástica, pero menos claridad sobre si la suplementación en individuos sin deficiencia (p. ej., veganos repletos o aquellos con niveles normales de B12) proporciona beneficio cognitivo o del estado de ánimo. Los resultados de neuropatía y cognición descansan en ensayos más pequeños y cortos a menudo en poblaciones específicas (diabéticos, pacientes con cáncer, ancianos con deterioro cognitivo); si los beneficios se generalizan a adultos más jóvenes o neuropatía aguda no se detalla. Los resultados del embarazo y posparto aparecen en solo algunos estudios; el neurodesarrollo infantil a largo plazo de la suplementación materna requiere seguimiento adicional. Ningún estudio recuperado examinó sistemáticamente la suplementación con B12 en personas con enfermedad renal, una población que puede acumular metabolitos inactivos de B12—la seguridad en insuficiencia renal permanece sin estudiar en los registros proporcionados.

appraisal_es.headline: La vitamina B12 tiene evidencia fuerte para tratar la deficiencia establecida/anemia megaloblástica, pero la evidencia de su uso más allá de los estados de deficiencia (cognición, neuropatía, estado de ánimo) se basa en un único metanálisis de 2021 que no ha sido replicado de forma independiente y los estudios siguen siendo pequeños y heterogéneos.

concerns.issue: Un único metanálisis no replicado impulsa múltiples resultados
concerns.detail: El metanálisis de 2021 (n=6276) aparece en la base de evidencia para cognición, función neurológica, estado de ánimo y resultados de fatiga. Para cognición y estado de ánimo específicamente, esta única síntesis es el ÚNICO metanálisis presente, y el motor explícitamente señala que 'su conclusión no ha sido replicada o verificada de forma independiente.' Cuatro ensayos controlados aleatorios apoyan cognición (n=120, 307, 400, y uno sin reportar), pero solo existe una revisión sistemática independiente para cualquier resultado más allá de deficiencia, creando una vulnerabilidad de cuello de botella.

concerns.issue: Tamaños de muestra pequeños en ensayos de neuropatía y estado de ánimo
concerns.detail: El resultado de neuropatía incluye solo 3 ensayos controlados aleatorios, con n reportados de 20, 90, y uno sin reportar (estudio de 1992). El resultado de estado de ánimo incluye solo 2 ensayos controlados aleatorios, con n=14 (1996) y 307 (2022, que está titulado sobre suplementación de B6, no B12). Un único valor atípico o un ensayo de alto riesgo podría cambiar la dirección o magnitud de los efectos, y n=14 es insuficientemente potente para detectar efectos modestos en el estado de ánimo.

concerns.issue: Los ensayos de deficiencia confunden el tratamiento de deficiencia con beneficio en poblaciones no deficientes
concerns.detail: La calificación 'Fuerte' para deficiencia de B12/anemia megaloblástica es apropiada—esta es una patología conocida con una justificación biológica clara. Sin embargo, muchos ensayos de cognición, neuropatía y estado de ánimo no especifican claramente el estado basal de B12 o restringen la inscripción a sujetos deficientes. Si los ensayos de cognición inscribieron pacientes con deficiencia cognitiva sin deficiencia confirmada de B12, el efecto podría no generalizarse a la suplementación en poblaciones repletadas. El motor no señala esta distinción en los resultados.

concerns.issue: El reporte de tamaño de muestra es incompleto y oscurece la verdadera precisión
concerns.detail: Para cognición, 4 de 6 estudios reportan n; para neuropatía, 6 de 14; para estado de ánimo, 3 de 3. El motor señala que 'la mayoría de resúmenes omiten tamaño de muestra, por lo que el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor,' pero esto significa que muchos estudios no pueden evaluarse individualmente por su adecuación. Una evaluación solo de resúmenes no puede evaluar el riesgo de sesgo por reporte selectivo de resultados ni distinguir entre ensayos pequeños insuficientemente potentes y adecuadamente potentes que simplemente no reportaron n en el resumen recuperado.

concerns.issue: Publicación muy reciente de ensayos controlados aleatorios clave sin seguimiento a largo plazo
concerns.detail: Para cognición, el ensayo controlado aleatorio de 2023 (n=307) es uno de solo cuatro ensayos primarios. Para neuropatía, dos ensayos controlados aleatorios de 2026 (n=20 y n=148) están entre la evidencia más reciente. No hay datos visibles de seguridad o eficacia a largo plazo en estos registros, y los ensayos muy recientes aún no han sido sometidos a replicación independiente. Las bases de cognición y neuropatía parecen ser rápidamente evolutivas en lugar de un consenso estable.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Para deficiencia de B12 y anemia megaloblástica, el mecanismo está bien establecido: B12 es esencial para la síntesis de ADN y la maduración de glóbulos rojos, y la deficiencia causa directamente eritropoyesis anormal. Esto apoya directamente la calificación Fuerte. Para cognición, neuropatía y estado de ánimo, el mecanismo es plausible pero indirecto: B12 es un cofactor para síntesis de mielina y reacciones de metilación, pero el salto clínico de 'B12 es necesario para la función nerviosa' a 'la suplementación de B12 mejora la neuropatía en pacientes no deficientes' o 'reduce la depresión' requiere evidencia de que estas condiciones son causadas por insuficiencia funcional de B12 más que por otra patología. La evidencia recuperada no establece claramente que la deficiencia basal esté presente en la mayoría de ensayos de cognición/estado de ánimo/neuropatía, haciendo el vínculo mecanismo-resultado inferencial en lugar de mecanístico.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que las calificaciones Moderada para cognición, neuropatía y estado de ánimo descansan principalmente en un único metanálisis de 2021 que sintetiza poblaciones heterogéneas (neuropatía diabética, deterioro cognitivo, depresión) sin documentar consistentemente el estado basal de B12, y no ha sido replicado de forma independiente. Los pequeños ensayos primarios (n=14, 20, 90 para estado de ánimo y neuropatía) son insuficientemente potentes, y varios parecen confundir el tratamiento de deficiencia con mejora en poblaciones repletadas. La base de evidencia en su conjunto muestra efectos fuertes cuando B12 es verdaderamente deficiente, pero evidencia débil y no replicada para suplementación más allá de estados de deficiencia, sugiriendo que las calificaciones para cognición/neuropatía/estado de ánimo podrían estar infladas por sobregeneralización a partir de datos de tratamiento de deficiencia.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Replicación independiente del metanálisis de 2021 por equipos separados de revisión sistemática, o al menos 2–3 nuevos ensayos controlados aleatorios adecuadamente potentes (n ≥200 por brazo) que explícitamente inscriban poblaciones no deficientes y pre-especifiquen el estado basal de B12, aclararía si la suplementación de B12 beneficia cognición, neuropatía o estado de ánimo fuera del contexto de deficiencia. Datos de seguimiento a largo plazo (≥1 año) para resultados de cognición y neuropatía también fortalecerían la confianza en la durabilidad.
